def solve_cvrp(instance):
    depot = instance["depot_index"]
    customers = list(instance["customer_ids"])
    demands = instance["demands"]
    capacity = instance["capacity"]
    matrix = instance["distance_matrix"]
    nn = instance.get("nearest_neighbors", None)
    hint = instance.get("vehicle_count_hint", None)

    if not customers:
        return []

    def route_demand(route):
        s = 0
        for n in route:
            s += demands[n]
        return s

    def route_cost(route):
        if not route:
            return 0
        c = matrix[depot][route[0]]
        for i in range(len(route) - 1):
            c += matrix[route[i]][route[i + 1]]
        c += matrix[route[-1]][depot]
        return c

            i += 1
            j -= 1

    # Start each customer in its own route
    routes = []
    route_of = {}  # node -> route index
    pos_in_route = {}  # node -> position index
    for c in customers:
        r = [c]
        idx = len(routes)
        routes.append(r)
        route_of[c] = idx
        pos_in_route[c] = 0

    # Precompute all savings pairs (i<j among customers) deterministically
    # savings(i,j)=d(depot,i)+d(depot,j)-d(i,j)
    # Use tie-breaker to keep deterministic order.
    savings = []
    for a_i in range(len(customers)):
        i = customers[a_i]
        di = matrix[depot][i]
        for a_j in range(a_i + 1, len(customers)):
            j = customers[a_j]
            s = di + matrix[depot][j] - matrix[i][j]
            # Store also reverse savings same magnitude; end-to-start depends on orientation, handled by endpoints.
            savings.append((s, i, j))
    savings.sort(key=lambda x: (x[0], -x[1], -x[2]), reverse=True)

    # Helper to get current endpoints and ensure route indices still valid (no merged routes left behind)
    active = [True] * len(routes)

    def get_endpoints(route_idx):
        r = routes[route_idx]
        if not r:
            return (None, None)
        return (r[0], r[-1])

    def can_merge(i, j, ri, rj):
        # merge route ri ending with i and route rj starting with j, or vice versa with reversal
        if not active[ri] or not active[rj] or ri == rj:
            return False, None
        ri_list = routes[ri]
        rj_list = routes[rj]
        if not ri_list or not rj_list:
            return False, None
        if ri_list[-1] != i:
            return False, None
        if rj_list[0] != j:
            return False, None
        if route_demand(ri_list) + route_demand(rj_list) <= capacity:
            return True, "end_to_start"
        return False, None

    def merge_routes(ri, rj, i, j):
        # Assumes ri ends with i and rj starts with j.
        # Connect: ri + rj
